podcasts.name: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Alt Rock Resurgence of 2004
podcast.body: The Yeah Yeah Yeahs, identified as "the Ye-Yaz," were named as one of the new and exciting bands contributing to the resurgence of Alt Rock by 2004. "By 2004, Alt Rock was back with all kinds of new exciting bands that was Franz Ferdinand and Modest Mouse and the Killers and Billy Towns and the Stills and Jet, the Ye-Yaz and Hot Hot Heat."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: 2017 Cassette Releases
podcast.body: The Yeah Yeah Yeahs were among many artists who saw numerous cassette releases in 2017, contributing to the format's contemporary resurgence. This period marked a significant increase in new music being issued on cassette. "en el 2017 hubo un montón de lanzamientos en caset los ya ya ya es la nada del rey randi ues."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Coleccionar Cassettes. Cosas que hay que saber.

podcast.title: Amazing Reputation and Academy Awards Connection
podcast.body: The Yeah Yeah Yeahs, a prominent band from the New York indie rock scene, have built an "amazing reputation" that extends beyond music, notably reaching the Academy Awards. This highlights their broad cultural impact and artistic acclaim. "The yay-yay-yes have an amazing reputation that extends through the Academy Awards."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 9: (20-11)

podcast.title: Embracing Cheap Instruments
podcast.body: The Yeah Yeah Yeahs are mentioned as an example of bands from the indie revival that embraced the use of inexpensive instruments as part of an anti-establishment image. This choice reflected a rejection of the high-end, vintage gear associated with earlier rock eras. "They wouldn't be caught dead playing, let's say a vintage-less paw, think white stripes, yeah, yeah, yeah, and the strokes and the black keys."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Story of the Electric Guitar - Part 3

podcast.title: Indie Rock Revival (2000s)
podcast.body: The Yeah Yeah Yeahs (transcribed as "the yay-y-yes") are cited as one of the new, "fresh sounding bands" that emerged during the Indie Rock Revival in the early 2000s.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Karen O as a Walking Billboard
podcast.body: Karen O, the highly charismatic front person of the Yeah Yeah Yeahs, became a willing "walking billboard" for New York designer Christian Joy. As the band gained popularity and Karen O became a photographed figure, the increased visibility of Christian Joy's designs led to a surge in orders, allowing the designer to leave her day job and pursue fashion full-time. "The Ye-E-S featuring senior Karen O who is dressed by an up-and-coming New York designer named Christian Joy. Karen has become a willing, walking billboard for Christian's work."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Million-Selling Debut
podcast.body: The Ye-Eyes' 2003 debut album was both a critical hit and a commercial success, selling around a million copies worldwide, highlighting the commercial potential of the Garage Rock revival. "And then in 2003, they released a debut album which was not only a critical hit, but also sold around a million copies worldwide."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 4: Garage Rock

podcast.title: New York Formation and Midwest Influences
podcast.body: Singer Karen O. and drummer Brian Chase met at college in Ohio in the late 1990s. They later moved to New York, where they met photographer and guitarist Nick Zinner. Their initial band, Unitarred, evolved its sound to incorporate the "trashy, punky Garage Rock" Karen O. heard in Ohio, drawing influences from Detroit (140 miles up I-90) and Cleveland (35 miles east on Highway 10), near Akron (home of The Pretenders and The Black Keys). "Singer Karen O. met drummer Brian Chase at College in Ohio in the late 1990s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 4: Garage Rock

podcast.title: Part of Indy Rock Revival
podcast.body: The Yeah Yeah Yeahs were explicitly named as a band that, alongside The Strokes, The White Stripes, Interpol, The Vines, The Hives, and Arcade Fire, was a firm part of the Indy Rock Revival in the late 2003/early 2004 period. "The strokes were firmly part of the Indy Rock Revival that also included the white stripes, the yay-yayas, interpole, the vines, the hives, and this new band called Arcade Fire."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pioneers of the Indie Rock Revival (Early 2000s)
podcast.body: The Yeah Yeah Yeahs were among the "new, sharp clever bands" that emerged during the Indie Rock Revival or Post-Punk Revival period around 2000-2001. This movement was a refurbished version of old-school early alt-rock, garage rock, and punk styles. "We gave us new, sharp clever bands like the strokes and the hives, the yay-yaz, friends ferdinand, interpool, and the arctic monkeys."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Toured with White Stripes and Strokes
podcast.body: After renaming themselves from Unitarred to The Ye-Eyes, the band quickly began touring with other prominent Garage Rock revival acts, The White Stripes and The Strokes. "Unitarred was renamed the Ye-Eyes and soon found themselves touring with the White Stripes and the Strux."

xref.title: Key Figure in New York Indie Rock Revival
xref.body: LCD Sound System became a prominent band in the New York indie rock revival, a scene that also featured groups such as The Strokes, Yeah Yeah Yeahs, and Interpol. "LCD Sound System was one of the leading lights of the New York indie rock revival that also included bands like The Strokes and The Ye-Ye-As and Interpol."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Motor City Ancestor
xref.body: Iggy Pop and the Stooges are cited as "Motor City ancestors" who influenced the Detroit and Michigan underground indie scene, especially inspiring bands like The White Stripes and Yeah Yeah Yeahs. "From there, they ingratiated themselves into the Detroit and Michigan underground indie scene, all of whom had something in common with motor city ancestors like the Stooges and the MC5."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: NYC Indie Scene Prominence
xref.body: TV on the Radio was a significant part of the New York City indie music scene in the early 2000s, a period that also saw the rise of bands like the Yeah Yeah Yeahs, The Strokes, The Rapture, and LCD Soundsystem. "TV on the radio was a major part of the New York City indie scene in the early 2000s. This was the same scene that gave us the yay-yayah as the strokes, the rapture and LCD sound system."
